course.title: General Professional
course.desc: Contracts, reports, data analysis, hiring — skills that apply to any profession.

exercises.title: Vague vs. precise
exercises.sc:
You need a summary of a 30-page vendor agreement. Here's what most people type:

"Summarize this contract."

The AI returns a generic overview that misses what you actually care about.
exercises.task: Write a better prompt. Be specific about: what sections matter, what format you want, and what details to highlight. Imagine the contract is between your company and a cloud hosting provider.
exercises.hint: The guide's principle: a 200-word specification produces better results than a 20-word instruction followed by 15 rounds of correction.
exercises.cr: 1) Specifies which sections to focus on 2) Defines output format 3) Mentions what to highlight or flag 4) Is substantially more detailed than 'summarize this contract'

exercises.title: Specify the output
exercises.sc: Your team lead asks you to "get the AI to analyze our Q3 sales data." You have numbers for 4 regions across 3 product lines, with month-by-month breakdowns.
exercises.task: Write a prompt that specifies exactly what the output should look like. Define the structure — table? Bullet points? What columns, metrics, comparisons?
exercises.hint: If you handed the output to your team lead, would they immediately know what they're looking at without follow-up questions?
exercises.cr: 1) Specifies output format explicitly 2) Names specific metrics 3) Requests comparisons 4) Defines what 'good' looks like

exercises.title: Audience and tone
exercises.sc:
Your company is switching from Slack to Microsoft Teams next month. You need to communicate this to:

1. The executive team (brief, strategic)
2. Department managers (operational)
3. All employees (friendly, reassuring)
exercises.task: Write a prompt for ONE audience that explicitly controls tone, length, and emphasis. Make it clear who the reader is and what they care about.
exercises.hint: Executives want the 'why' in two sentences. Employees want to know 'what changes for me.'
exercises.cr: 1) Clearly identifies target audience 2) Specifies tone 3) Defines what to emphasize vs. omit 4) Sets length expectations 5) Shows audience-aware framing

exercises.title: Setting constraints
exercises.sc: You're asking the AI to draft a client-facing project proposal. Without constraints, the AI produces either a 200-word stub or a 2,000-word essay with speculative claims.
exercises.task: Write a prompt with explicit constraints: word count range, what NOT to include, required sections, formatting rules, and compliance requirements.
exercises.hint: Telling the AI what to avoid is just as valuable as telling it what to do.
exercises.cr: 1) Sets specific length constraint 2) Includes 'do not' instructions 3) Lists required sections 4) Mentions formatting rules 5) Demonstrates negative constraints

exercises.title: Role assignment
exercises.sc: You need the AI to review a marketing email before it goes out. You could just say "review this email" — but the feedback depends on what perspective the AI takes.
exercises.task: Write a prompt that assigns the AI a specific role (e.g., "You are a senior copywriter with 15 years of B2B SaaS experience"). Define what expertise to apply.
exercises.hint: A 'compliance officer' catches different things than a 'brand strategist.'
exercises.cr: 1) Assigns a specific role with credentials 2) Defines what expertise to apply 3) Specifies what to evaluate 4) Role choice meaningfully shapes feedback

exercises.title: Iterative refinement
exercises.sc:
You asked the AI for a project status update and got:

"The project is progressing well. We completed the design phase and are moving into development. Some minor delays occurred but the team is addressing them."

Generic, vague, embarrassing in a meeting.
exercises.task: Write a follow-up prompt that fixes this. Don't start over — refine. Tell the AI specifically what's wrong and what to change.
exercises.hint: Good refinement is surgical: 'The delays section needs specifics — mention the API integration delay (3 days).' Bad: 'Make it better.'
exercises.cr: 1) References specific problems 2) Gives targeted corrections 3) Adds missing specifics 4) Shows refinement over restarting 5) Demonstrates iterate cycle

exercises.title: Plan before you ask
exercises.sc:
You need a comprehensive market research report on AI adoption in your industry. If you just say "write a market research report," you'll get mediocre results.

The guide's core principle: spend 10 minutes planning to save an hour of corrections.
exercises.task: Write a detailed specification prompt (150-250 words). Include: purpose, target reader, required sections, data sources, formatting, length, and exclusions.
exercises.hint: Your specification IS the prompt. The more precise the spec, the better the first output.
exercises.cr: 1) Defines purpose and reader 2) Lists specific sections 3) Specifies data sources 4) Sets length and format 5) Includes exclusions 6) Spec itself is 100+ words

exercises.title: Chain-of-thought
exercises.sc: A job applicant submitted a resume for Senior Marketing Manager. Requirements: 5+ years B2B marketing, marketing automation tools, team management, $1M+ pipeline campaigns.
exercises.task: Write a prompt forcing step-by-step thinking: first extract qualifications, then compare against each requirement, then score, then recommend. Use explicit step numbering.
exercises.hint: Chain-of-thought: 'Before giving your answer, first do X, then Y, then Z.' Reasoning improves dramatically with sequential steps.
exercises.cr: 1) Uses explicit numbered steps 2) Separates extraction from evaluation 3) Asks for reasoning before conclusions 4) Includes scoring system 5) Steps build logically

exercises.title: Few-shot examples
exercises.sc:
You're building a system to categorize support tickets: Billing Issue, Technical Bug, Feature Request, Account Access, General Inquiry.

Examples:
• "I was charged twice" → Billing Issue
• "App crashes uploading files over 10MB" → Technical Bug
• "Can you add dark mode?" → Feature Request
exercises.task: Write a prompt using few-shot examples that teaches the AI to categorize new tickets. Include examples in consistent format, define all categories, add 2-3 test cases.
exercises.hint: Format consistency matters: if examples use '→', use '→' for all of them.
exercises.cr: 1) Includes 3+ clear example pairs 2) Defines all categories 3) Examples cover multiple categories 4) Includes new test cases 5) Consistent format

exercises.title: Structured output
exercises.sc:
You've asked the AI to analyze a vendor contract. Instead of a wall of text, you want a structured risk assessment:

| Clause | Section | Risk Level | Finding | Recommendation |
exercises.task: Write a prompt that enforces specific output structure. Define exact columns, what goes in each, risk level criteria, and how to handle edge cases.
exercises.hint: Show the exact format you want. Include an example row if possible.
exercises.cr: 1) Defines exact structure 2) Explains each column 3) Provides risk criteria 4) Handles edge cases 5) Optionally includes example row

exercises.title: Compare and evaluate
exercises.sc:
The AI wrote two product descriptions:

A: "Our platform streamlines workflow management with cutting-edge AI technology, enabling unprecedented productivity gains."

B: "Teams using our platform close tasks 40% faster by automating handoffs between design, engineering, and QA — no workflow diagrams needed."
exercises.task: Write a prompt that evaluates both against specific criteria and picks a winner. Define 3-4 criteria, ask for per-criterion scores, require justified recommendation.
exercises.hint: Don't ask 'which is better?' Instead: 'Score each 1-5 on clarity, specificity, emotional impact, and CTA strength.'
exercises.cr: 1) Defines 3+ criteria 2) Asks for per-criterion scores 3) Requires reasoning 4) Requests justified recommendation 5) Meaningful non-overlapping criteria

exercises.title: Multi-step decomposition
exercises.sc:
CEO asks: "Competitive analysis of our top 3 competitors, SWOT for each, and positioning recommendations."

Too big for one prompt. Needs decomposition.
exercises.task: Write a SEQUENCE of 3-4 prompts that decompose this. Each builds on the previous output. Show the full chain.
exercises.hint: Workflow: Research → Structure → Analyze → Synthesize. Each step has clear input and output.
exercises.cr: 1) Breaks into 3+ sequential prompts 2) Each has focused objective 3) Later prompts reference earlier outputs 4) Covers data→analysis→synthesis 5) Demonstrates decomposition

exercises.title: Error correction
exercises.sc:
The AI produced this churn analysis:

"Churn increased 15%, primarily driven by pricing changes. Main affected segment: enterprise. Recommendation: reduce prices 20%."

Problems: single-factor, simplistic recommendation, correlation as causation.
exercises.task: Write a prompt correcting these errors. Ask for multi-factor analysis, distinguish correlation from causation, provide nuanced recommendations.
exercises.hint: Point out exactly what's wrong: 'You assumed pricing caused churn without considering onboarding quality, support times, or competitors.'
exercises.cr: 1) Identifies specific errors 2) Asks for multi-factor analysis 3) Addresses correlation vs causation 4) Requests nuanced recommendations 5) Shows critical thinking

exercises.title: Persona prompting
exercises.sc:
Stress-test a business proposal from three perspectives:

1. Skeptical CFO (financial viability)
2. Customer advocate (user impact)
3. Risk manager (operational vulnerabilities)
exercises.task: Write a prompt that has the AI adopt each persona sequentially, critique the proposal, then synthesize into a unified risk assessment.
exercises.hint: Each persona surfaces different concerns. CFO: ROI. Customer advocate: friction. Risk manager: what could go wrong.
exercises.cr: 1) Defines 3 distinct personas 2) Each has specific concerns 3) Sequential analysis 4) Requests synthesis 5) Shows how persona shapes analysis

exercises.title: Prompt templates
exercises.sc: You review customer feedback weekly: categorize, summarize, create action items. Instead of writing a new prompt each time, you want a reusable template.
exercises.task: Create a reusable prompt template with [BRACKET] variables. Include: data source, time period, categories, output format, recipient. Should work for any week.
exercises.hint: Variables like [TIME_PERIOD], [CATEGORY_LIST], [RECIPIENT] make it reusable — like the CLAUDE.md skills from the guide.
exercises.cr: 1) Uses clear bracket variables 2) Genuinely reusable 3) Covers input/processing/output/recipient 4) 4+ variable placeholders 5) Would save time weekly

exercises.title: Contract analysis
exercises.sc: You have a 15-page vendor agreement for cloud hosting. Boss needs a risk assessment by EOD. Key concerns: liability caps, GDPR compliance, termination, auto-renewal, pricing escalation.
exercises.task: Write a prompt producing a structured contract analysis: clause categories, risk levels with criteria, table with clause references, warning flags.
exercises.hint: Structure your prompt like a professional checklist: what to extract, how to assess, how to present.
exercises.cr: 1) Lists clause categories 2) Defines risk criteria 3) Specifies table output 4) Includes warning mechanism 5) Covers key concerns 6) Professional output

exercises.title: Email triage
exercises.sc: 127 unread emails after a week-long vacation. You need to identify what's urgent, what needs response, and what to archive.
exercises.task: Write a prompt that categorizes emails by urgency and required action. Define categories, urgency criteria, and a scannable output format.
exercises.hint: Priority Matrix: Urgent+Important, Important+Not Urgent, Urgent+Not Important, Neither.
exercises.cr: 1) Defines triage categories 2) Specifies urgency criteria 3) Distinguishes respond/delegate/archive 4) Scannable output 5) Practical time-saver

exercises.title: Meeting notes
exercises.sc: 90-minute product planning meeting. Topics: Q4 feature prioritization, enterprise client bug, new hire onboarding, budget reallocation. Decisions made, action items assigned.
exercises.task: Write a prompt transforming rough notes into structured minutes: sections, action items with owners and deadlines, handling ambiguity.
exercises.hint: Template: Header, Decisions, Action Items, Discussion Summary, Next Steps.
exercises.cr: 1) Defines output sections 2) Action items have owner + deadline 3) Handles ambiguity 4) Prioritizes decisions over discussion 5) File naming mentioned

exercises.title: Data comparison
exercises.sc:
Business vehicle options:
• Lease BMW 320d ($650/mo, 36mo, 12k mi/yr)
• Buy used Toyota Camry ($22k, 5.9% over 48mo)
• Car allowance $500/month

Need 3-year total cost comparison.
exercises.task: Write a prompt for structured financial comparison: time horizon, all cost categories, explicit assumptions, recommendation format.
exercises.hint: Include: maintenance, insurance, tax deductions, residual value, total out-of-pocket. State all assumptions.
exercises.cr: 1) All cost categories 2) Clear timeframe 3) Explicit assumptions 4) Summary comparison table 5) Recommendation with reasoning 6) Tax dimension

exercises.title: Report drafting
exercises.sc: CEO wants a 5-page AI adoption report for the board. Data-driven, forward-looking, with company-specific recommendations.
exercises.task: Write the specification prompt — the detailed brief for a board-ready report on the first try. Structure, length per section, data requirements, tone, exclusions.
exercises.hint: This is the ultimate 'plan before you ask' exercise. 200-word spec > 20-word instruction + 15 corrections.
exercises.cr: 1) Defines structure 2) Length per section 3) Data/source requirements 4) Board-level tone 5) Exclusions 6) Spec is 150+ words 7) Would produce board-ready output

exercises.title: Policy change comms
exercises.sc:
Remote work reduced from 4 to 2 days/week next month. Unpopular. Need:
1. Internal memo to all staff
2. FAQ for employee concerns
3. Manager talking points
exercises.task: Write one prompt producing all three documents with different tones but consistent messaging. Address the sensitive nature.
exercises.hint: Facts identical across documents, framing changes. FAQ must address real concerns honestly.
exercises.cr: 1) Requests all three 2) Different tones each 3) Consistent facts 4) Addresses concerns authentically 5) Handles pushback 6) Strategic communication

exercises.title: Resume screening
exercises.sc: Hiring Senior Data Analyst: SQL, BI tools (Tableau/Power BI), 3+ years analytics, stakeholder presentation skills. 12 resumes to screen, shortlist top 4.
exercises.task: Write a prompt creating systematic screening: scored criteria with weights, must-have vs nice-to-have, red flags, shortlist output format.
exercises.hint: Chain-of-thought: extract qualifications → score against criteria → rank → recommend. Weighted scoring prevents gut-feel.
exercises.cr: 1) Scored criteria with weights 2) Must-haves vs nice-to-haves 3) Red flags 4) Comparison table 5) Reasoning behind rankings 6) Multiple techniques combined

exercises.title: Feedback classification
exercises.sc:
200+ customer feedback entries from support, app reviews, social media, NPS. Need to:
1. Categorize
2. Identify trends
3. Prioritize fixes
4. Report to product team
exercises.task: Write a comprehensive prompt for this end-to-end pipeline. Use few-shot for categorization, chain-of-thought for trends, structured output for the report.
exercises.hint: Capstone: combine every technique. Few-shot + structured output + chain-of-thought + planning.
exercises.cr: 1) Few-shot examples 2) Clear categories 3) Trend identification 4) Prioritization criteria 5) Structured report 6) 3+ techniques combined 7) Reusable workflow

CLOUD HOSTING SERVICE AGREEMENT (Excerpt)

Section 4.2 - Service Level Agreement
Provider guarantees 99.9% uptime monthly. Credits: 10% fee for 99.5-99.9%, 25% for 95-99.5%, 100% below 95%.

Section 7.1 - Limitation of Liability
Provider's total liability shall not exceed fees paid in preceding 12 months. No liability for indirect, consequential damages.

Section 9.3 - Data Processing
All data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3). Customer retains data ownership. Provider may access for support/maintenance only.

Section 11.2 - Termination
Either party: 30 days written notice. Immediate if material breach unremedied for 15 days. Customer data export available 30 days post-termination.

Section 12.5 - Auto-Renewal
Agreement renews annually unless notice given 60 days before term end. Pricing may increase up to 8% per year with 90-day notice.

materials.11:
PRODUCT DESCRIPTION A
"Our platform streamlines workflow management with cutting-edge AI technology, enabling unprecedented productivity gains."

PRODUCT DESCRIPTION B
"Teams using our platform close tasks 40% faster by automating handoffs between design, engineering, and QA — no workflow diagrams needed."

EVALUATION CRITERIA:
1. Clarity - Is the benefit immediately clear?
2. Specificity - Does it use concrete details vs. vague claims?
3. Credibility - Would a skeptical buyer believe this?
4. Customer-centricity - Is it about them or about us?

materials.20:
AI ADOPTION REPORT - REQUIREMENTS

Audience: Board of Directors
Length: 5 pages (executive summary + 4 sections)
Tone: Data-driven, strategic, forward-looking
Purpose: Inform Q2 AI investment decisions ($500K budget)

Required sections:
1. Executive Summary (0.5 pages)
2. Current State: AI use internally (1 page)  
3. Market Analysis: Competitor AI capabilities (1.5 pages)
4. Opportunities: Where AI adds value (1.5 pages)
5. Recommendations: Specific investments + ROI (0.5 pages)

Data sources:
- Internal usage surveys (IT dept has data)
- Gartner/Forrester industry reports
- Competitor analysis (marketing has intel)
- Customer feedback on AI features

- No vendor comparisons (procurement team handles)
- No timeline >12 months out
